note: Closed variety of code shapes that swallow a failure a user would meet (G2-14, AR-1, FR-13). Read by scripts/user_path_failures.py, which matches line by line and never decides whether a place is on a user path: the requirements tester does. A match is `start` on a line, `quiet` in the next `window_lines` lines (the line itself counts) and `loud` in none of them. Every pattern is a Python regular expression; a line starting a comment never starts a match. A new language or a new shape is a new row here, never a second list in code. A row that does not compile is named as not measured, the others still run.

patterns.why: an error is caught and only logged or dropped, so the user sees nothing happen (the window is lines, not the block: read the block)
a response is read as a success without looking at its status, so a failed call looks like a good answer
a request is sent and its answer is never looked at, so a failed call goes on as a success (a 500 does not throw)
